page: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 is a compute-oriented virtual server within the Dls v5 series, powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 64 vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, accompanied by 128 GB of RAM. This configuration provides 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU, representing a 1:2 ratio that prioritizes raw compute capacity over memory volume. The server contains no local storage and includes zero GPUs, utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization to attach remote storage volumes.

Benchmark results show upper-quartile multi-threaded processing power, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 16569.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 60731.27. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 292.88 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 135.25 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the top 25 percent. In hardware-accelerated operations, the platform achieves 58517.16 in PassMark encryption due to AES and VAES instruction sets. Single-core performance falls in the median range, with Geekbench single-core at 1671.0 and stress-ng single-core at 1900.1.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio presents tradeoffs for memory-intensive applications, and the lack of local NVMe storage necessitates external network storage for disk operations. Furthermore, execution of large language models shows performance constraints, generating only 2.77 tokens per second on a 70B parameter model. Given its hardware balance and high static web serving throughput of 53.15 GB/sec, the instance is appropriate for multi-threaded software compilation, batch compute pipelines, and CPU-heavy web serving.
description: The Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 is a compute-oriented virtual machine equipped with 64 vCPUs and 128 GB of system memory, driven by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor at 2.8 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with hyper-threading across 32 physical cores, it delivers a 1:2 core-to-memory profile tailored for compute-heavy applications. The instance contains no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight upper-tier multi-threaded processing, evidenced by strong results in PassMark CPU calculations, Clang compilation, and uncached large-block memory bandwidth exceeding 292 GB/sec. Single-core throughput and standard compression tasks perform at median industry levels, while large-model LLM inference shows substantial computational limitations. The absence of onboard disks requires networked storage solutions. Overall, the configuration provides efficient resource allocation for parallel computational workloads, multi-threaded software builds, high-throughput static web serving, and distributed batch processing pipelines requiring substantial CPU allocation without proportional memory expense.
